examples.en: Standardizing package sizes lowered the shipping cost.
Once things are standardized, parts are easy to swap.

examples.ko: 모든 교실을 똑같이 만드는 규격화는 좋지 않다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I don't think making every classroom the same through standardization is good.

examples.ko: 회사는 제품 규격화를 위해 새 기준을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The company created new standards for product standardization.

examples.ko: 규격화 덕분에 어느 충전기나 다 맞아요.
examples.en: Thanks to standardization, any charger fits.
Many people also oppose excessive standardization.

explain: 물건의 크기나 부품에 쓰면 편리하다는 중립적인 느낌이에요. 사람, 교육, 문화에 쓰면 틀에 박혀 똑같아진다는 부정적인 느낌이 생겨요. 비슷한 말 '표준화'와 달리 크기와 모양 같은 눈에 보이는 기준을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: For sizes and parts it sounds neutral and convenient. Used for people, education, or culture it takes on a negative feel of being squeezed into the same mold. Unlike '표준화', it fits well when talking about visible standards like size and shape.

examples.en: The company standardized the size of all its parts.
If you standardize packing boxes, logistics costs go down.

examples.ko: 교육을 너무 규격화해서는 안 된다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think education shouldn't be standardized too much.
Someone suggested standardizing the charging ports.
Thanks to standardizing the product, repairs became easier.

examples.ko: 크기를 규격화해도 디자인은 다양하게 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even if you standardize the size, you can make the designs varied.

explain: '~을/를 규격화하다'로 써요. 물건의 크기나 모양을 기준에 맞춘다는 점에서 '표준화하다'와 가깝지만, 사람이나 교육에 쓰면 개성을 없앤다는 부정적인 느낌이 생겨요.
explain_en: It is used as '~을/를 규격화하다'. It is close to '표준화하다' in fitting size or shape to a standard, but when applied to people or education it takes on a negative feel of erasing individuality.

examples.en: Break the problem down into small parts and solve it.
The school divides students into finer groups by level.
If you divide the team in detail by role, work gets easier.
Please don't split the menu into too many categories.
The app has divided the notification types into finer categories.
I'm going to break the budget down by item.

explain: '나누다'보다 이미 나눈 것을 더 잘게 쪼갠다는 느낌이 있어요. '~을/를 세분화하다' 꼴로 쓰고, 분류·업무·예산·시장처럼 체계가 있는 대상에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Compared with '나누다', it feels like cutting something already divided into finer pieces. It is used as '~을/를 세분화하다' and suits organized things such as categories, tasks, budgets and markets.

examples.ko: 이 발표에서는 자료의 시각화가 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: In this presentation, visualizing the data is the most important part.

examples.ko: 시각화 도구를 쓰면 보고서가 훨씬 깔끔해져요.
examples.en: If you use a visualization tool, the report becomes much neater.

examples.ko: 목표의 시각화는 동기 부여에 도움이 된대요.
examples.en: I heard that visualizing your goals helps with motivation.

examples.ko: 복잡한 숫자는 시각화를 거쳐 그래프로 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The complicated numbers went through visualization and were shown as graphs.

examples.ko: 지도 시각화 덕분에 사고 지역이 한눈에 보여요.
examples.en: Thanks to the map visualization, the accident areas are visible at a glance.
The visualization work alone took two days.

explain: 숫자나 정보를 그래프, 그림, 지도로 보기 쉽게 나타내는 것을 말해요. 회사 보고서, 데이터 수업, 발표에서 많이 들어요. 머릿속에 목표를 그려 보는 것도 시각화라고 해요.
explain_en: It means showing numbers or information in an easy-to-see form such as graphs, pictures or maps. You hear it in company reports, data classes and presentations. Picturing a goal in your head is also called 시각화.

examples.en: I completed all the required courses at university.
If you complete this course, you get a certificate.
To graduate, you have to earn forty credits.

examples.ko: 교육을 이수한 사람만 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who have completed the training can take the exam.

examples.ko: 한 학기에 최대 스무 학점까지 이수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take up to twenty credits in one semester.
I completed the lectures online and received a confirmation letter.

explain: '과목, 과정, 학점, 교육'처럼 정해진 공부를 목적어로 받아요. 아무 일이나 끝낼 때 쓰는 '끝내다'와는 달라요. 학교에서는 '필수 이수', '이수 학점'이라는 말을 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It takes objects like courses, credits, or training, meaning you finish a set program of study. Unlike '끝내다', it is not for finishing just anything. At school you will often see '필수 이수' and '이수 학점'.

p.n: 이수 means earning the required credits; 수료 means finishing the program.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 서비스를 분야별로 전문화하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our company decided to specialize its services by field.
The hospital specialized its departments starting this year.

examples.ko: 작은 가게는 한 가지 메뉴만 전문화해서 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The small shop gained popularity by specializing in just one menu item.

examples.ko: 교육 과정을 전문화하려고 강사를 새로 뽑았어요.
examples.en: They hired new instructors to make the curriculum more specialized.
If you specialize the work, efficiency goes up.
If you don't specialize, it's hard to survive the competition.

explain: '~을 전문화하다'처럼 한 분야를 좁혀 깊이 있게 만든다는 뜻으로 쓰고, 회사나 가게, 학교 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 작은 회사에서 여러 일을 하는 것과 달리 한 가지를 깊이 한다는 느낌이에요. '전문화'라는 명사 형태로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used as '~을 전문화하다' to mean narrowing a field and making it deeper, and it often comes up when talking about companies, shops and schools. It contrasts with doing many jobs at a small company by focusing deeply on one. The noun form '전문화' is also very common.

examples.en: Please refer to the manual.
It's easy to understand if you refer to the picture.

examples.ko: 저는 다른 글을 참조해서 보고서를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote the report by referring to other writing.
For details, please see the table below.
It's good to consult several sources.

examples.ko: 그 자료를 참조했는데도 답을 못 찾았어요.
examples.en: I looked at that material but still couldn't find the answer.

explain: '참조하다'는 '확인하세요' 대신 안내문, 설명서, 보고서에서 자주 써요. '보세요'보다 글로 쓴 말투이고, 일상 대화에서는 '참고하다'를 더 많이 말해요. 이메일의 '참조(CC)'도 같은 한자어예요.
explain_en: 참조하다 appears in notices, manuals and reports to say 'see this'. It sounds more written than 보세요, and in daily talk 참고하다 is more common. The email field 참조 (CC) uses the same word.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 두 장을 합성한 거예요.
examples.en: This photo is a composite of two pictures.
I tried combining face photos with an app.

examples.ko: 두 물질을 합성하면 새로운 재료가 돼요.
examples.en: If you synthesize two substances, you get a new material.
I'm learning how to composite videos.
They synthesized a voice to make the announcement.
I can't tell if it's a composite picture or a real one.

explain: 여러 개를 합쳐 하나로 만든다는 말인데, 사진·영상·소리·화학 물질에 쓰여요. 일상에서는 사진 합성이 가장 흔해요. 그냥 '합치다'와 달리 새로운 결과물이 나온다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means combining several things into one, used for photos, video, sound, and chemical substances. In daily life, photo compositing is the most common use. Unlike plain '합치다', it implies a new product comes out.
